summary: Attempt 4 repairs the two required changes recorded in review-003 and leaves every other reviewed element of the change untouched. (1) The T006 import-graph gate is green again: ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2 now declares, in both rows that carried the non-canonical string 'backtest / presentation / reports', the layer the layer map assigns — the T063 row (line 119) and the T105 row (line 155) read 'backtest / research', which canonicalises to the map's 'backtest' for robinhood_lp.reports.{manifest,metrics,rerun,run_identity,validation}. The T105 row no longer lists robinhood_lp.__main__ as a module it declares, because MODULE_OVERRIDES classifies that module as application / orchestration; the row records in prose that the artifact-rerun entry is extended through the application / orchestration CLI surface that T097 maps, so the row cannot disagree with the map even if its annotated task cell is later normalised to a bare task id. A sentence after the table states the rule that a row declares only the layer of the modules it names, so a later amendment cannot reintroduce the defect. (2) This record states that spec_revision was raised by this amendment from v1-2026-09-20-admission-write-boundary-and-threat-owners to v1-2026-09-20-strategy-successor-ownership and why, correcting the contradicting sentence in the attempt-3 record, which this layer may not edit. No task, contract, dependency, revision value or impact-ledger entry changes in this attempt, and the ten previously recorded impacts are carried forward unchanged.
rationale: The review measured that the attempt-3 candidate left the repository red on a gate that was green at the base: tools/check_imports/layer_map.py:140 classifies robinhood_lp.reports as 'backtest', LAYER_ALIASES has no entry for 'backtest / presentation / reports', and canonical_layer(declared) != classify(module) therefore fired five architecture-disagreement findings at ARCHITECTURE.md:119, failing tests/test_import_graph.py, which pytest runs as the CI quality gate. tools/check_imports/layer_map.py is outside every role's and every layer's write surface, so the repair cannot be made on the map side: a §2.2 row may only declare a layer the map assigns to the modules it names. 'backtest / research' is that declaration — it canonicalises to 'backtest', it is the §2.1 tier line whose own scope already names manifests, and the neighbouring T064, T066 and T101 rows already use it. Applying the same repair to line 155 exposed one further latent disagreement that the review had counted only in part: the T105 row also named robinhood_lp.__main__, which MODULE_OVERRIDES classifies as application / orchestration, so a row declaring one layer while naming modules from two would still fire a finding the moment its task cell is normalised. Because a §2.2 row carries exactly one layer, the T105 module cell now names only the modules of that layer and the CLI surface is described in prose instead of being assigned a layer that is not its own; the added sentence states the rule so the defect class, not just its two instances, is closed. The second required change cannot be applied where the review pointed, and this is recorded rather than worked around: todo/amendments/A0014/prophet-003.json is written by the controller from the author's structured result and is not a path the PROPHET layer may edit — finish-amendment refuses any changed path outside docs/spec/, docs/intent/, docs/implement/, the listed root documents, a phase README, the added task contracts and the config entries for added tasks. The correction is therefore stated in this attempt's record, which supersedes the earlier one and names the wrong sentence explicitly, and prophet-003.json is left unedited as the historical record of attempt 3.

impact_assessment.intent: Unchanged and not restated. This attempt touches no file under docs/intent/, and intent_revision stays v1-2026-09-20-backtest-runs-and-permission-entry: measured against the freeze base 1aa6f45, the field is byte-identical and only the four tasks T105-T108 plus spec_revision differ in todo/config.yaml. A0014 still implements the already-confirmed G-STRATEGY-REGISTRY-01 and G-BACKTEST-RUN-01 direction through four successor tasks; attempt 4 adds no goal, no product choice, no pool or chain decision, and no risk or live-policy change.
impact_assessment.specification: spec_revision IS raised by this amendment, and this attempt keeps that raised value: todo/config.yaml moved from v1-2026-09-20-admission-write-boundary-and-threat-owners to v1-2026-09-20-strategy-successor-ownership because A0014 edits docs/spec/ — ARCHITECTURE.md, ADR-003-configuration-and-secrets.md and THREAT_MODEL.md — and the PROPHET layer may change both revisions. The attempt-3 record's sentence that 'Intent and spec_revision remain unchanged' contradicted its own diff and is corrected here; intent_revision is genuinely unchanged because docs/intent/ was not touched. This attempt edits exactly one document, docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md, and changes no revision value in todo/config.yaml (it changes nothing in that file at all): the T063 and T105 rows now declare 'backtest / research', the layer the layer map assigns to robinhood_lp.reports.*, which restores the T006 §2.2 agreement gate that the attempt-3 string broke. The raised value still names the spec state this amendment produces, so it is not moved again for a repair inside the same edit; no product behaviour, requirement clause or unresolved choice changed, and the ownership and fail-closed transition statements reviewed in attempt 3 are untouched.
impact_assessment.contracts: Unchanged from attempt 3: exactly four new contracts — T105 replaces T063, T106 replaces T064, T107 replaces T066 and T108 replaces T067 — and no contract that existed before A0014 is edited by any attempt; this attempt edits no contract at all. Ten existing PLANNED contracts still require a later CONTRACT amendment (T068, T069, T073, T083, T084, T087, T088, T096, T101, T102); each is recorded below under its own stable impact ID, and T096 must additionally carry the independently reviewed evidence of all four successors.
impact_assessment.dependencies: Unchanged and re-measured against todo/config.yaml: T105=[T063,T068], T106=[T064,T068,T105], T107=[T065,T066,T068,T105,T106], T108=[T067,T068,T105]; the graph is acyclic, and the proposed rewiring keeps it acyclic while bringing all four successors into T096's closure. T096's closure is 53 tasks, contains T063, T064 and T066, and contains none of T105-T108; T108 has no ordinary PLANNED consumer, which is why it needs an explicit T096 dependency. Direct PLANNED dependents of the retiring predecessors are T068, T069, T073, T084 and T101 on T063 and T073 and T083 on T066; T064 and T067 have only their successors T106 and T108. This attempt changes no dependency and no config field, so the reviewed rewiring stands exactly as recorded.
impact_assessment.implementation: This attempt changes one documentation file. ARCHITECTURE §2.2 declares the map-assigned layer for the T063 and T105 rows, and the T105 row names only robinhood_lp.reports.{manifest,validation,rerun,run_identity,metrics} — the modules the map classifies as backtest — while its artifact-rerun entry point, which lives in the robinhood_lp.__main__ CLI surface that the map classifies as application / orchestration and the T097 row already maps, is described in prose. A sentence after the table states that a row declares only the layer of the modules it names, so the T006 gate cannot be broken again by the same pattern. Successor implementation ownership is otherwise as reviewed in attempt 3: T105 governs current robinhood_lp.reports publication and rerun, T106 the robustness surfaces, runner and reports, T107 the experiments search and candidate lock, and T108 the authoring guide, its example and drift tests. No business implementation or test file is touched by this amendment.
impact_assessment.data: Not applicable to this attempt: it changes no persisted schema, manifest, report, artifact, lock, checksum, configuration value or operational record — only the layer string of two documentation rows and one explanatory sentence. The reviewed account stands: existing T063/T064/T066 manifests, reports, surfaces, locks, rejected runs, checksums and review artifacts remain byte-for-byte read-only; new artifacts bind registry/schema identity, version and checksum; missing bindings are explicit legacy state, never inferred or backfilled, and any migration is additive, retains the source checksum and provenance, and cannot turn prior test-fold exposure into a fresh candidate.
impact_assessment.operations: Not applicable to this attempt: no running or deployed process, operator control, rollout order or rollback behaviour is affected by correcting a documentation layer string, and todo/config.yaml is not modified so no task state, attempt, commit or revision moves. The reviewed cutover order stands unchanged — T068 registry, then T105 manifest, then T106 robustness, then T107 candidate lock, with T108 following T068 and T105 — together with its fail-closed publication and rollback rules and the boundary that T069 alone owns durable run state, cancellation and restart while rerun-manifest remains an artifact operation unless invoked through a new T069 run record.
impact_assessment.security: No security effect beyond the reviewed A0014 assessment: this attempt grants, removes and re-scopes no permission, authorisation, secret boundary or signing path, and it edits only prose and a layer label in ARCHITECTURE.md. The reviewed statements stand unchanged — registry and schema metadata grant no approval, risk, signer, execution or live authority; T087/T088 and T084 remain read or control surfaces that cannot rewrite provenance and cannot bypass central risk; the T067 guide's transition notice rejects notes and display text as an identity source; and the A0014 transition rule makes an unapproved successor unavailable after predecessor retirement rather than permitting a fail-open fallback.
impact_assessment.verification: Author-side checks run inside the amendment worktree — investigation only, never acceptance evidence, and no substitute for an independent review. The gate this repair targets: python -m tools.check_imports check --suppressions docs/implement/ci/suppressions.toml --config todo/config.yaml --architecture docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md prints 'import-graph check passed: no findings' with exit status 0, where the attempt-3 candidate produced five architecture-disagreement findings at ARCHITECTURE.md:119; a scan of every §2.2 row, including rows whose task cell is annotated and therefore skipped by the checker, reports zero declared-layer/classification mismatches, so the same defect no longer exists in latent form anywhere in the table. python -m pytest tests/test_import_graph.py tests/test_documentation_citations.py tests/test_documentation_links.py is 37 passed; the full suite is 2316 passed, 6 skipped, 1 failed. tools.check_citations check, tools.check_acceptance check, ruff check and ruff format --check report no findings, and python -m tools.workflow validate returns OK. The single failure, tests/test_abi_artifacts.py::test_artifact_byte_matches_regenerated_oracle_output, is pre-existing and environmental — forge aborts with 'tools/oracle/lib/v4-core/src/libraries/TickMath.sol: No such file or directory' because the vendored Solidity libraries are not checked in, and the same failure was measured at the review base — and a Markdown-only diff cannot reach it. mypy could not be run in this worktree: the conda environment's editable install resolves robinhood_lp to a different worktree, so mypy stops with a module-resolution error in tests/_storage_t031_fixtures.py before checking anything; this attempt contains no Python file, so the mypy gate cannot depend on it. The successor evidence obligations are unchanged: each of T105-T108 requires positive, negative, compatibility, migration and old-path-unreachable coverage, and the independent Developer and Reviewer evidence for those tasks remains outstanding.

affected_existing_tasks.reason: T068 currently depends on T063 and says it modifies the T063 manifest path. T105 is now the designated registry-bound manifest successor and depends on T068, so replacing T063 with T105 inside T068 would create a cycle while leaving T063 would strand an ordinary PLANNED consumer on a retired predecessor. The contract must identify T068 as the registry producer and T105 as the downstream integration owner rather than claiming the old manifest as its dependency.
affected_existing_tasks.required_disposition: CONTRACT: revise T068 to preserve registry/schema/provenance delivery while moving current manifest binding and its integration acceptance to T105. DEPENDENCY: remove T063 and do not add T105, because T105 depends on T068. IMPLEMENTATION: T068 may expose deterministic registry validation but must not establish a second manifest publisher; T105 performs cutover from the old validator. DATA: registry records are new and deterministic; historical manifests are handled by T105, not rewritten by T068. OPERATIONS: registry must be available before T105 cutover; missing registry fails closed. SECURITY: unchanged—no RPC/storage/signer/Web import or authority. VERIFICATION: test registry behavior locally and let T105 prove manifest integration and old-path unreachability.

affected_existing_tasks.reason: T069 depends on and repeatedly names T063 as the manifest/report producer. After T105 becomes current, that text and dependency would route product runs to the retired hard-coded identity path and omit the explicit rerun-manifest versus product-run lifecycle boundary.
affected_existing_tasks.required_disposition: CONTRACT/DEPENDENCY: replace T063 with T105 and cite T105's registry-bound manifest plus rerun boundary. IMPLEMENTATION: every product run publishes through T105; artifact rerun remains separate, while a product rerun creates a new durable T069 run linked to the source manifest. DATA: preserve source manifests read-only and link rather than overwrite. OPERATIONS: retain queued/running/failed/cancelled/succeeded, restart and no-partial-result semantics. SECURITY: no new permission or secret surface. VERIFICATION: cover new run, linked rerun, cancellation/failure and rejection of legacy/unregistered inputs.

affected_existing_tasks.reason: T073 directly depends on T063 and T066 and presents their backtest evidence and provisional candidate during Owner authorization. Those dependencies would be forbidden after retirement and could display legacy identity-unbound evidence or a candidate lock that does not freeze registry/schema revision.

IMPLEMENTATION: authorization views read only current T105/T107 artifacts; legacy artifacts remain historical and visibly non-current. DATA: retain old evidence read-only and never copy it into a new authorization. OPERATIONS: fail closed if current manifest/lock is absent or mismatched; existing pool/token/paper authorization order remains. SECURITY: registration is not authorization and T073 remains the Owner write boundary. VERIFICATION: positive current-evidence display plus negative legacy, mismatch and downgrade cases.

affected_existing_tasks.reason: T083 directly depends on T066. Retiring T066 without rewiring leaves a normal PLANNED consumer on the old candidate lock, whose frozen fields do not bind registry identity, schema and revision.
affected_existing_tasks.required_disposition: CONTRACT/DEPENDENCY: replace T066 with T107 and use T107's candidate/version identity wherever readiness or evidence is consumed. OPERATIONS: missing/mismatched/downgraded locks block rather than fall back. SECURITY: the lock grants no live permission; existing risk and promotion boundaries remain. VERIFICATION: cover current lock, old-format rejection, mismatch and unavailable-revision behavior.
